units.left_text: After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked of the LORD, saying, “Who should go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”
units.right_text: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”

units.left_text: The LORD said, “Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.”
units.right_text: “Judah shall go up,” answered the LORD. “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.”

units.left_text: Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with you into your lot.” So Simeon went with him.
units.right_text: Then the men of Judah said to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” So the Simeonites went with them.

units.left_text: Judah went up, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand. They struck ten thousand men in Bezek.
units.right_text: When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.

units.left_text: They found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and they fought against him. They struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
units.right_text: And there they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, striking down the Canaanites and Perizzites.

units.left_text: But Adoni-Bezek fled. They pursued him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

units.left_text: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their big toes cut off, scavenged under my table. As I have done, so God has done to me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
units.right_text: Then Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” And they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.

units.left_text: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
units.right_text: Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.

units.left_text: After that, the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, and in the South, and in the lowland.
units.right_text: Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.

units.left_text: Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron. (The name of Hebron before that was Kiriath Arba.) They struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
units.right_text: Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron (formerly known as Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

units.left_text: From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir. (The name of Debir before that was Kiriath Sepher.)
units.right_text: From there they marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).

units.left_text: Caleb said, “I will give Achsah my daughter as wife to the man who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it.”
units.right_text: And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”

units.left_text: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it, so he gave him Achsah his daughter as his wife.
units.right_text: So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.

units.left_text: When she came, she got him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey; and Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”
units.right_text: One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”

units.left_text: She said to him, “Give me a blessing; because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” Then Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
units.right_text: “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.”

units.left_text: The children of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and they went and lived with the people.
units.right_text: Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad. They went to live among the people.

units.left_text: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. The name of the city was called Hormah.
units.right_text: Then the men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites, attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath, and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.

units.left_text: Also Judah took Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.
units.right_text: And Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron — each with its territory.

units.left_text: The LORD was with Judah, and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
units.right_text: The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.

units.left_text: They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove the three sons of Anak out of there.
units.right_text: Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, who drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.

units.left_text: The children of Benjamin didn’t drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
units.right_text: The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.

units.left_text: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
units.right_text: The house of Joseph also attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

units.left_text: The house of Joseph sent to spy out Bethel. (The name of the city before that was Luz.)
units.right_text: They sent spies to Bethel (formerly known as Luz),

units.left_text: The watchers saw a man come out of the city, and they said to him, “Please show us the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with you.”
units.right_text: and when the spies saw a man coming out of the city, they said to him, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.”

units.left_text: He showed them the entrance into the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man and all his family go.
units.right_text: So the man showed them the entrance to the city, and they put the city to the sword but released that man and all his family.

units.left_text: The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day.
units.right_text: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day.

units.left_text: Manasseh didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shean and its towns, nor Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
units.right_text: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.

units.left_text: When Israel had grown strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, and didn’t utterly drive them out.
units.right_text: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.

units.left_text: Ephraim didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, but the Canaanites lived in Gezer among them.
units.right_text: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.

units.left_text: Zebulun didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites lived among them, and became subject to forced labor.
units.right_text: Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.

units.left_text: Asher didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;
units.right_text: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.

units.left_text: but the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they didn’t drive them out.
units.right_text: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

units.left_text: Naphtali didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth Anath; but he lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh and of Beth Anath became subject to forced labor.
units.right_text: Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.

units.left_text: The Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill country, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley;
units.right_text: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.

units.left_text: but the Amorites would dwell in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. Yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became subject to forced labor.
units.right_text: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.

units.left_text: The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.
units.right_text: And the border of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.

units.left_text: The LORD’s angel came up from Gilgal to Bochim. He said, “I brought you out of Egypt, and have brought you to the land which I swore to give your fathers. I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you.
units.right_text: Now the angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land that I had promised to your fathers, and I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you,

units.left_text: You shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land. You shall break down their altars.’ But you have not listened to my voice. Why have you done this?
units.right_text: and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.’

units.left_text: Therefore I also said, ‘I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.’”
units.right_text: So now I tell you that I will not drive out these people before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.”

units.left_text: When the LORD’s angel spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people lifted up their voice and wept.
units.right_text: When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.

units.left_text: They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
units.right_text: So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.

units.left_text: Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the children of Israel each went to his inheritance to possess the land.
units.right_text: After Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites went out to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.

units.left_text: The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the LORD that he had worked for Israel.
units.right_text: And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.

units.left_text: Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred ten years old.
units.right_text: And Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.

units.left_text: They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
units.right_text: They buried him in the land of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

units.left_text: After all that generation were gathered to their fathers, another generation arose after them who didn’t know the LORD, nor the work which he had done for Israel.
units.right_text: After that whole generation had also been gathered to their fathers, another generation rose up who did not know the LORD or the works that He had done for Israel.

units.left_text: The children of Israel did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and served the Baals.
units.right_text: And the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals.

units.left_text: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the peoples who were around them, and bowed themselves down to them; and they provoked the LORD to anger.
units.right_text: Thus they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they followed after various gods of the peoples around them. They bowed down to them and provoked the LORD to anger,

units.left_text: They abandoned the LORD, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
units.right_text: for they forsook Him and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.

units.left_text: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of raiders who plundered them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
units.right_text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He delivered them into the hands of those who plundered them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, whom they were no longer able to resist.

units.left_text: Wherever they went out, the LORD’s hand was against them for evil, as the LORD had spoken, and as the LORD had sworn to them; and they were very distressed.
units.right_text: Wherever Israel marched out, the hand of the LORD was against them to bring calamity, just as He had sworn to them. So they were greatly distressed.

units.left_text: The LORD raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them.
units.right_text: Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.

units.left_text: Yet they didn’t listen to their judges; for they prostituted themselves to other gods, and bowed themselves down to them. They quickly turned away from the way in which their fathers walked, obeying the LORD’s commandments. They didn’t do so.
units.right_text: Israel, however, did not listen to their judges. Instead, they prostituted themselves with other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned from the way of their fathers, who had walked in obedience to the LORD’s commandments; they did not do as their fathers had done.

units.left_text: When the LORD raised up judges for them, then the LORD was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for it grieved the LORD because of their groaning by reason of those who oppressed them and troubled them.
units.right_text: Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for the Israelites, He was with that judge and saved them from the hands of their enemies while the judge was still alive; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppressed them and afflicted them.

units.left_text: But when the judge was dead, they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers in following other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They didn’t cease what they were doing, or give up their stubborn ways.
units.right_text: But when the judge died, the Israelites became even more corrupt than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They would not give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.

units.left_text: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel; and he said, “Because this nation transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not listened to my voice,
units.right_text: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He said, “Because this nation has transgressed the covenant I laid down for their fathers and has not heeded My voice,

units.left_text: I also will no longer drive out any of the nations that Joshua left when he died from before them;
units.right_text: I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.

units.left_text: that by them I may test Israel, to see if they will keep the LORD’s way to walk therein, as their fathers kept it, or not.”
units.right_text: In this way I will test whether Israel will keep the way of the LORD by walking in it as their fathers did.”

units.left_text: So the LORD left those nations, without driving them out hastily. He didn’t deliver them into Joshua’s hand.
units.right_text: That is why the LORD had left those nations in place and had not driven them out immediately by delivering them into the hand of Joshua.

units.left_text: Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to test Israel by them, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
units.right_text: These are the nations that the LORD left to test all the Israelites who had not known any of the wars in Canaan,

units.left_text: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at least those who knew nothing of it before:
units.right_text: if only to teach warfare to the subsequent generations of Israel, especially to those who had not known it formerly:

units.left_text: the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
units.right_text: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.

units.left_text: They were left to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the LORD’s commandments, which he commanded their fathers by Moses.
units.right_text: These nations were left to test the Israelites, to find out whether they would keep the commandments of the LORD, which He had given their fathers through Moses.

units.left_text: The children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
units.right_text: Thus the Israelites continued to live among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

units.left_text: They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons and served their gods.
units.right_text: And they took the daughters of these people in marriage, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

units.left_text: The children of Israel did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and forgot the LORD their God, and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
units.right_text: So the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.

units.left_text: Therefore the LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the children of Israel served Cushan Rishathaim eight years.
units.right_text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him eight years.

units.left_text: When the children of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a savior to the children of Israel, who saved them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
units.right_text: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.

units.left_text: The LORD’s Spirit came on him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war, and the LORD delivered Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. His hand prevailed against Cushan Rishathaim.
units.right_text: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel’s judge and went out to war. And the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into the hand of Othniel, who prevailed against him.

units.left_text: The land had rest forty years, then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
units.right_text: So the land had rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.

units.left_text: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, and the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in the LORD’s sight.
units.right_text: Once again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. So He gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.

units.left_text: He gathered the children of Ammon and Amalek to himself; and he went and struck Israel, and they possessed the city of palm trees.
units.right_text: After enlisting the Ammonites and Amalekites to join forces with him, Eglon attacked and defeated Israel, taking possession of the City of Palms.

units.left_text: The children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.
units.right_text: The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.

units.left_text: But when the children of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a savior for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
units.right_text: And again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer. So they sent him with tribute to Eglon king of Moab.

units.left_text: Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
units.right_text: Now Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his cloak

units.left_text: He offered the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
units.right_text: and brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was an obese man.

units.left_text: When Ehud had finished offering the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.
units.right_text: After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he ushered out those who had carried it.

units.left_text: But he himself turned back from the stone idols that were by Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”
units.right_text: But upon reaching the idols near Gilgal, he himself turned back and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”

units.left_text: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
units.right_text: Then Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in the coolness of his upper room. “I have a word from God for you,” Ehud said, and the king rose from his seat.

units.left_text: Ehud put out his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body.
units.right_text: And Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon’s belly.

units.left_text: The handle also went in after the blade; and the fat closed on the blade, for he didn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.
units.right_text: Even the handle sank in after the blade, and Eglon’s fat closed in over it, so that Ehud did not withdraw the sword from his belly. And Eglon’s bowels emptied.

units.left_text: Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
units.right_text: Then Ehud went out through the porch, closing and locking the doors of the upper room behind him.

units.left_text: After he had gone, his servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, “Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.”
units.right_text: After Ehud was gone, Eglon’s servants came in and found the doors of the upper room locked. “He must be relieving himself in the cool room,” they said.

units.left_text: They waited until they were ashamed; and behold, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen down dead on the floor.
units.right_text: So they waited until they became worried and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upper room. Then they took the key and opened the doors— and there was their lord lying dead on the floor.

units.left_text: Ehud escaped while they waited, passed beyond the stone idols, and escaped to Seirah.
units.right_text: Ehud, however, had escaped while the servants waited. He passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.

units.left_text: When he had come, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he led them.
units.right_text: On arriving in Seirah, he blew the ram’s horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him from the hills, and he became their leader.

units.left_text: He said to them, “Follow me; for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They followed him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
units.right_text: “Follow me,” he told them, “for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.”

units.left_text: They struck at that time about ten thousand men of Moab, every strong man and every man of valor. No man escaped.
units.right_text: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men. Not one of them escaped.

units.left_text: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. Then the land had rest eighty years.
units.right_text: So Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel that day, and the land had rest for eighty years.

units.left_text: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. He also saved Israel.
units.right_text: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. And he too saved Israel, striking down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.

units.left_text: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight, when Ehud was dead.
units.right_text: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the sight of the LORD.

units.left_text: The LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
units.right_text: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his forces was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

units.left_text: The children of Israel cried to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and he mightily oppressed the children of Israel for twenty years.
units.right_text: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, because Jabin had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he had harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years.

units.left_text: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.
units.right_text: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.

units.left_text: She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
units.right_text: And she would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.

units.left_text: She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali, and said to him, “Hasn’t the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded, ‘Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
units.right_text: She summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, “Surely the LORD, the God of Israel, is commanding you: ‘Go and march to Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.

units.left_text: I will draw to you, to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into your hand.’”
